paragraphs.source_en: Early the next morning, Tenkai unexpectedly took his leave and drifted away.

paragraphs.source_en: At first, Itakura Katsushige considered sending someone to follow him, but the sight of his departing figure made him abandon the idea. Perhaps because he was accustomed to traveling alone, there was not the slightest air of loneliness or destitution about Tenkai's receding figure. Whatever villains he encountered would probably take him for no more than a roadside tree or stone. He was truly a man to inspire both reverence and fear. If Katsushige had him followed, Tenkai would likely laugh at him for still failing to understand what sort of man he was.

paragraphs.source_en: Leaving Katsushige's residence, Tenkai leisurely raised his eyes toward the castle on his right and walked on. As he neared the gate of Zōjōji, he suddenly decided to skirt the temple and go to Takanawa, then turn left at Yatsuyama and head toward Shinagawa. He found the conversation of the porters and horse drivers traveling alongside him highly amusing.

paragraphs.source_zh: 天海出了胜重的宅子，悠然抬头看了看右首的城池，走了出去。快到增上寺山门时，他突然决定绕过增上寺去高轮，再由八山左转到品川方向。他觉得，同行的搬运人夫和马夫的谈话很是有趣。

paragraphs.source_en: The porters said that a few steps farther on, when they reached the shore by Bell Forest, there would be women who shared travelers' beds. Yet women were so scarce in Edo now that they would never spare a glance for mere porters or horse drivers. Wealthy samurai would court them instead, and any jealous rivalry was certain to end in violence.

paragraphs.source_en: At Odawara he had dismissed his splendid procession. Now his retinue was very modest, comprising only some twenty mounted samurai and just over thirty foot soldiers. Ieyasu's stout body was wedged into the palanquin, and he looked distinctly uncomfortable. Though both side doors of the palanquin stood open, sweat still streamed from his brow. Anyone unaware of his identity would surely have taken him for a daimyō with an estate of thirty or fifty thousand koku out on a journey.

paragraphs.source_en: Zon'ō and Tenkai had known each other for twenty years. They had met before the Battle of Mikatagahara, when both were traveling with their books in pursuit of learning. At that time Tenkai still called himself Zuifū. He met Zon'ō at Renkeiji in Kawagoe, Musashi Province, where Zon'ō was already a disciple of the priest Zonjō of that temple. The two often argued so fiercely that spittle flew, though neither could now remember what they had debated in those days. Yet by the time they parted, each had come to feel a profound affinity with the other.

paragraphs.source_en: After becoming abbot of the Tokugawa family temple, Zon'ō insisted that Tenkai meet Ieyasu, and it was for that reason that Tenkai had now come to Edo. Compared with Hideyoshi, of course, he conveyed a far greater sense of solidity and candor. Yet this very Tokugawa Ieyasu had returned with anguish written across his face.
